title: Marbled Soy Tea Eggs
summary: A Chinese-style snack of hard-boiled eggs simmered in a spiced soy broth, then cracked and steeped so the whites turn beautifully marbled. Savoury, lightly salty, and ideal for make-ahead snacking.
steps: Place the eggs in a saucepan and cover with enough water to come 2 cm above them. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 9 minutes until hard-boiled.
Drain the eggs and cool them under cold running water. Gently tap the shells all over with the back of a spoon so the shells crack but stay on the eggs.
In the same pan, combine the water, soy sauce, salt, sugar, ginger, bay leaves, cinnamon, and black pepper. Bring to a simmer and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the cracked eggs to the simmering liquid and keep them just below a boil for 10 minutes to flavour the whites.
Turn off the heat and leave the eggs to steep in the liquid for at least 45 minutes, or ideally overnight in the fridge, for a deeper colour and stronger flavour.
Peel the eggs to reveal the marbled pattern and serve chilled or at room temperature.
